body:
Spec for epic #1, revision 2. Lock = @dharishan04 approves the latest push.

## Agent summary
Amended specs/1.md to revision 2. I added FR-007: sensor IDs that name JS object prototype members (`__proto__`, `constructor`, `toString`, …) answer 404 `{"error":"unknown_sensor"}` on both `/history` and `/latest`. I added FR-007 to milestone #2's covers and added a dated Clarifications line for r2. Everything else from r1 is unchanged. The new case file is `app/cases/1/prototype-ids.spec.ts` (covers FR-007). It checks five IDs (`__proto__`, `constructor`, `toString`, `hasOwnProperty`, `valueOf`) on both endpoints, 10 tests in all. Each one asserts the exact 404 status and the `unknown_sensor` body, so the app's generic `not_found` 404 can't satisfy them. `app/openapi.yaml` is untouched, since the note didn't ask for it.

**Tests:** I ran `npx playwright test cases/1/prototype-ids` from `app/`. All 10 new tests fail. The `/latest` ones fail because the endpoint answers 200 instead of 404 for these IDs. I only read the output for the `valueOf` `/latest` test (Expected 404, Received 200) and assumed the other `/latest` tests fail the same way. I didn't read the `/history` failures. That route doesn't exist yet, so they most likely return the generic `not_found` body. I didn't run the r1 history cases.

title: Spec 1 r1: I wrote `specs/1.md` (revision 1) and `app/cases/1/history.s
body:
Spec for epic #1, revision 1. Lock = @dharishan04 approves the latest push.

## Agent summary
I wrote `specs/1.md` (revision 1) and `app/cases/1/history.spec.ts`. The spec still has one `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]`, so Lock will be refused until the lead answers it.

**Requirements**
- **FR-001:** `GET /sensors/{id}/history?from&to` returns 200 with `{ sensorId, readings: [{ at, value }] }`, containing only that sensor's readings in the range, oldest first.
- **FR-002:** Both bounds are inclusive.
- **FR-003:** An unknown sensor returns 404 with `{ "error": "unknown_sensor" }`.
- **FR-004:** A range over the maximum returns 400 with `{ "error": "range_too_large" }`.
- **SC-001:** One day of an hourly sensor returns exactly 25 readings in ascending order.
- Milestone #2 covers all of these.

**Cases:** each of the five tests in `history.spec.ts` covers one item.
- Readings in range, oldest first, bounds inclusive: FR-001 and FR-002.
- Readings outside the range excluded: FR-001.
- A full day of hourly readings gives 25 in ascending order: SC-001.
- Unknown sensor: FR-003. It asserts the exact error body, so the app's generic `not_found` 404 can't satisfy it.
- Range over the limit: FR-004.

**Decisions I made:**
- I chose the response shape, the error code `range_too_large` and the inclusive bounds myself. They are noted under Clarifications.
- I didn't change `openapi.yaml`, because the lead's note didn't ask for it.
- Malformed or missing `from`/`to`, and `from` after `to`, are out of scope.

**Tests:** I ran `npx playwright test cases/1`. All 5 tests fail because the history route doesn't exist yet: they get the generic 404 `not_found` instead of the expected response. None fail on syntax errors.

**Open questions:**
- What is the maximum allowed range for /history (for example 7 or 31 days)? This is the one NEEDS CLARIFICATION in FR-004. The cases hold for any limit between 1 day and about 4 years.

## Agent summary
I amended `specs/1.md` (still revision 1) and `app/cases/1/history.spec.ts` for the lead's round-1 answers, and added the endpoint to `app/openapi.yaml`.

Requirements:
- **FR-001:** `GET /sensors/{id}/history?from&to` returns `{sensorId, readings[{at, value}]}`, only that sensor's readings, oldest first.
- **FR-002:** both bounds are inclusive.
- **FR-003:** an unknown sensor gets 404 `{error:"unknown_sensor"}`.
- **FR-004:** a range over 7 days gets 400 `range_too_large`, and exactly 7 days is accepted. The `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` marker is gone, and the 7-day limit is recorded under Clarifications dated 2026-10-20.
- **FR-005 (new):** an in-range window with no readings returns 200 with an empty array.
- **FR-006 (new):** the endpoint is documented in `app/openapi.yaml`, with the response schema and the 400 and 404 errors (new `History` schema).
- **SC-001:** a full day of hourly readings gives 25 readings in ascending order.

Clarifications also say that error precedence and timestamp formats are out of scope, along with missing/malformed bounds and `from` after `to`.

Cases (all in `app/cases/1/history.spec.ts`; the spec's `cases` and `milestones` front matter now cover FR-001 to FR-006 and SC-001):
- **FR-001, FR-002:** the original range case (inclusive bounds, oldest first) and the "excludes readings outside the range" case.
- **SC-001:** the full-day case.
- **FR-001 (new):** only the requested sensor's readings. s-1 and s-2 get the same timestamps and different values.
- **FR-005 (new):** a window with no readings returns `{sensorId, readings: []}`.
- **FR-004 (new):** exactly 7 days is accepted (169 readings), and 7 days plus 1 second gets 400 `range_too_large`.
- **FR-003:** an unknown sensor gets 404 with the exact body.
- **FR-004:** the existing over-the-limit case, a 4-year range.
- **FR-006:** no Playwright case. It is a documentation requirement.

One command was blocked by the delivery guard, which said `app/cases/1` is a locked case file. It had only mentioned that path in a read-only `ls`. I reran the inspection without it, and the later `Edit` to the case file went through. If the guard should have stopped that edit, the case-file change needs a second look.

**Tests:** `cd app && npx playwright test cases/1`: 9 of 9 fail today. The cases get a 404 `not_found` from the missing route, so the status or exact-body assertions fail. Nothing fails on a syntax error.

**Open questions:**
- Was the guard's "locked case file" block a false positive on the read-only `ls`? The later edit to `app/cases/1/history.spec.ts` was allowed, which suggests it was.
- FR-006 has no Playwright case, since it is a documentation requirement. It is attached to milestone #2 for coverage. Say if you want a different check for it.
